core_obligations: Construct O_2[F] as the sheafification of the free presheaf and the displayed relation map.
Set Omega = cokernel of the relation map and d(f) = image of [f]; check d is a derivation by construction.
For a derivation D, descend [g] ↦ D(g) to alpha_D: Omega → F using the defining properties of derivations.
Verify D = alpha_D ∘ d, giving the representing object (Omega, d).
proof_roadmap: free-sheaf construction + relation cokernel + universal descent via derivation axioms
difficulty_reason: Fully explicit construction: O_2[F] is the sheafification of the free presheaf, the displayed relation map (equation-define-module-differentials) encodes additivity, the Leibniz rule and the annihilation of the O_1-image, Omega is its cokernel, and d is induced by [f]; d is a derivation by construction (the relations are exactly the defining identities of a derivation), every derivation D gives the O_2-linear map [g] ↦ D(g) which kills the relation image by the defining properties, hence descends to alpha_D with D = alpha_D ∘ d, and the opening 'proved in exactly the same way as in algebra' is a framing sentence - the construction and all checks stand alone in the span.
